plan.title: Refactor
plan.why: Improve an area without changing behavior, backed by a baseline and a green verification path.
plan.what:
## Scope

- State the area to simplify and the behavior that must not change.
- List the non-goals and the constraints.

## Commit strategy

- Baseline, refactor, verify, and document in separate green commits.

milestones.title: Refactor the area
milestones.desc:
Outcome: As a maintainer, I want the area simplified, so that future changes are cheaper.

Scope: In scope: the named area and the behavior it must preserve. Out of scope: new behavior and unrelated cleanup.

Inputs: A baseline suite and the scouted area.

Slices: Baseline, simplify, verify, and document in separate green commits.

tasks.title: Establish the baseline
tasks.desc:
Approach: Name the tests and checks that prove current behavior.

Touch: tests/

Inputs: The area under refactor and its current verification command.

Commit: One baseline slice that pins current behavior.

Verify: The baseline suite passes before the change.

Guardrails: Do not change production behavior in the baseline slice.

tasks.title: Refactor the area
tasks.desc:
Approach: Name the structural change and the behavior that stays fixed.

Touch: src/

Inputs: The green baseline and the scouted structural change.

Commit: One refactor slice with no behavior change.

Verify: The baseline suite passes after the change.

Guardrails: Stop when a simplification cannot be proved behavior-preserving.

tasks.title: Test that behavior is unchanged
tasks.desc:
Approach: Run the baseline plus the nearest integration checks.

Touch: tests/

Inputs: The refactor slice and the baseline.

Commit: One verification slice for any missing coverage.

Verify: Every baseline check and the nearest integration checks pass.

Guardrails: Do not loosen the baseline to make the refactor pass.

tasks.title: Update the documentation
tasks.desc:
Approach: Record the new structure where maintainers will look.

Touch: docs/

Inputs: The final structure and its verification commands.

Commit: One documentation slice.

Verify: Links and examples resolve against the shipped structure.

Guardrails: Do not describe behavior the refactor did not change.
